mechanism: Bictegravir is a substrate of UGT1A1 and has minimal CYP450 involvement; scopolamine is metabolized via hydrolysis and CYP3A4, with no significant direct metabolic interaction, but additive anticholinergic effects are possible.
action: Monitor for anticholinergic adverse effects (dry mouth, urinary retention, constipation, CNS effects); no dose adjustment required but clinical observation recommended.
